deferred_source_units.reason: This unit contains the song-and-psalm attribution to Asaph. The general heading alone did not establish a particular literary relationship or an identifiable occasion; no historical Asaph identity was inferred.

The native coalition-list unit names Idumeans, Ishmaelites, Moab and Hagarenes. Its precise coalition and occasion are not established by the differently composed force in the read Chronicles account; the proposed historical identification remains a separate unretained candidate.

This continuation names Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, foreigners and Tyre inhabitants. No sufficiently particular account identifying this combination and its counsel was established; shared people names or generic warfare alone would not identify the episode.

The actual continuation has the valley of weeping, movement toward an appointed place and blessings given by the lawgiver. No sufficiently particular counterpart to this combination was established; familiar springs or rainfall were not supplied to replace the wording.

The unit asks the Lord God of powers and God of Jacob to hear prayer. A particular relationship beyond these common divine addresses and an ordinary request for hearing was not established in this pass.

The source is the general heading for the end and for the sons of Korah. Its broad attribution and designation alone do not establish a particular occasion or a sufficiently distinctive heading comparison.

The heading names a prayer for David and the petition asks hearing because the speaker is poor and needy. No particular Davidic episode or sufficiently specific counterpart beyond the widespread hearing-and-need formula was established.

This unit requests mercy and promises crying to God all day. A sufficiently particular correspondence beyond that common petition and duration was not established; an unexpressed occasion was not assigned.

The source asks God to give ear to the prayer and attend to the voice of petition. No sufficiently particular relationship beyond the ordinary vocabulary of requesting divine hearing was established in this pass.

Raab, Babylon, foreigners, Tyre and Ethiopians appear with a statement that these were born there. The antecedent and identities needed for a particular historical or birth-register comparison remain uncertain; Raab was not silently renamed Egypt and the birthplace was not supplied.

The petition asks that prayer enter before God and that He incline His ear. No particular correspondence beyond common language for a prayer being received was established, and the speaker or occasion was not identified from the heading.

The speaker describes poverty and toils from youth and says that after being raised up he was humbled and left helpless. No particular counterpart to that actual sequence was established; a royal biography or a different order of exaltation and humiliation was not supplied.

The heading identifies understanding and Ethan the Israelite without ancestry or an occasion. The independently read Ethan and Gaithan entries do not resolve which person is intended; those proposed identities are separately preserved at zero credit.

The unit combines an address to the Lord God of powers, a question of incomparability, divine might and surrounding truth. No additional particular relationship beyond these broad praise expressions was established; surrounding truth was not changed into a different attribute.

The enemies reproach the exchange of the anointed. The meaning of exchange and the precise object of the reproach remain unresolved; the read mockery of Jesus does not establish the proposed identification or justify replacing exchange with footsteps.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the hostile coalition
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The source list begins with Idumeans, Ishmaelites, Moab and Hagarenes and continues with further peoples. Chronicles describes a differently composed force against Jehoshaphat. Shared regional enemies do not establish that these are the same coalition or that the psalm describes this battle; the full ensuing battle context was read.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identity of Heman the Israelite
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The heading names Heman the Israelite without a patronymic. Chronicles names Heman the psalm singer with Joel and Samuel in his ancestry, and its surrounding genealogy places him among the Kaathites. Musical association and the shared name do not by themselves establish this precise identification; the additional Heman entry in 1 Chronicles 2:6 was also read.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identity of Ethan the Israelite
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The heading supplies Ethan the Israelite but no ancestry. Chronicles places its Ethan, son of Kisai, in the Merarite singers genealogy. The shared name does not resolve the heading against the Ethan listed among Zara's sons in 1 Chronicles 2:6-8; neither identity is credited.

The actual Kings unit names Gaithan the Ezraite among people surpassed by Solomon in wisdom, whereas the psalm names Ethan the Israelite. The name and designation differ, and the contexts do not establish an identity. Familiar wording from another edition was not substituted.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the proud defeated figure
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The psalm humbles an unnamed proud one like a wounded man. The actual Isaiah address is to Jerusalem, speaks of her arm and then of making the sea desolate and its depths a crossing road; it does not name Rahab or describe the anticipated wounded proud figure. Those familiar details cannot resolve an identity from the supplied texts.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the reproached exchange
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The psalm speaks of enemies reproaching the exchange of the anointed, an expression not resolved by its context. Matthew records abuse of Jesus and mockery that calls Him King of Israel, but does not explain that exchange. An identification of the psalmic event with this Passion scene is therefore unretained.

The proposed comparison anticipated dung language in Jeremiah 8:2. The complete actual text instead calls the unburied bones an example upon the earth's surface. That anticipated verbal correspondence is absent, and the En-dor victims are not identified with these bones. The distinct supported dung-image target is Jeremiah 32:33.

The source calls the Holy One of Israel our King. The actual Isaiah clause says the Lord God, the Holy One, presented Israel as your king; it does not supply the anticipated same divine-kingship predication. The original proposal is unretained rather than normalized; the separately read Isaiah 44:6 expressly calls God Israel's King.

precision_notes: All source words, original complete units, continuation paragraphs and supplied numbering are preserved; familiar Hebrew or English Psalm wording and numbering were not imported.

Limited literary and image comparisons do not assert identical historical events. The coalition identification, Heman and Ethan identities, and the reproached exchange remain separate unretained candidates or source deferrals.

The source retains the turtledove, the lawgiver, God appearing in Zion, being cast aside, inward speech, the heart rejoicing to fear, Mother Zion, physicians, and acquaintances removed because of misery.
Psalm 88 retains plural chosen ones, north and seas, the unnamed proud one, consecrated thing, fortifications made cowardice, removal from purification and the exchange of the anointed.
David, his offspring and Israel remain distinct recipients in the royal promises. Samuel as a historical actor is distinguished from the books named 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel.

Two attempted wording correspondences were not present in the actual targets: Jeremiah 8:2 has an example rather than dung; Isaiah 43:15 presents Israel as king. Their separate precise supported targets are Jeremiah 32:33 and Isaiah 44:6.
Two unavailable Revelation locator hints remain unread and zero credit, separately archived and excluded from the eight actual read candidates and from all target-unit counts.

All 28 source, target, candidate and context books have this author's own fresh full raw bodies and HTTP headers at the pinned commit, verified against Git blob identities and complete cached JSON. Pin checks themselves earn no semantic credit.

The community failed in divine anger and was troubled in wrath. No particular historical judgment is identified by those general experiences, even within the Moses-attributed prayer.
The years are pondered like a spider in the supplied text. This is not replaced with a sigh or an assumed web, and the read Bildad candidate describes a different spider-web construction.
The line asks how to number Thy right hand and refers to those bound in heart in wisdom. It is not rewritten as a request to number our days to create a familiar cross-reference.
The servants, God's works and guidance of their children are preserved. No identified episode or sufficiently particular separate counterpart for this combination is established.

Splendor upon the community and direction of the work of its hands remain the petition. The expected Proverbs 16:3 unit is absent in this edition, and a general work-and-blessing theme does not establish an alternative precise relation.
The thing passing through darkness, calamity and demon of noon are kept as supplied. No target identifies that noon demon or warrants replacing the language with an expected pestilence formulation.
The stated thousand and ten thousand falling on different sides do not identify a particular battle or plague. The assurance is not assigned a narrative solely from its general protection motif.
The Sabbath designation supplies no named performance or performers. The read Levitical-service candidate does not identify this particular song as the one performed.

The senseless person's inability to understand points forward to the following account of wicked flourishing and destruction. No separate link is retained merely from a general ignorance-and-wisdom contrast.
The everlasting Most High confession is preserved without adding a separate target on the basis of the general divine-exaltation theme alone.
The eye looked upon enemies and the ear will hear of evildoers rising against the speaker. Their downfall is not inserted into either sensory statement to create a triumph correspondence.
The continuing question about uttering injustice and the speech of workers of lawlessness does not provide a more particular independent counterpart than the common theme of wrongful speech.

The call for senseless people to understand and fools to become wise is retained as the transition to the creator-of-senses argument. A generic wisdom invitation is insufficient for a separate supported pair.
The question about the discipliner of nations and teacher of human knowledge is preserved. No separate link is assigned from divine teaching or rebuke as a broad theme.

The soothing from evil days until a pit is dug for the sinner does not state who digs it. It is not equated with a wrongdoer falling into his own trap, and no sufficiently precise independent comparison is retained.

Righteousness returning to judgment and upright hearts clinging to it are kept in their supplied construction. An ordinary justice-and-righteousness theme does not resolve the precise temporal and relational wording.
The questions about an ally rising and standing against evildoers identify no historical helper or particular encounter. General requests for assistance do not provide a sufficiently distinct match.

The pains in the heart and consolations loving the soul are preserved without replacing the latter verb with a familiar delight formulation. A general divine-comfort passage is not retained on that theme alone.
The combined summons to bow, fall and weep before the Maker is preserved. Weep is not changed to kneel, and a generic worship command alone is not an independent specific counterpart.
Divine greatness in Zion and exaltation above peoples are preserved without adding another pair merely from the broad Zion-praise theme.
The crooked heart did not cling, and the evil one turned away from the speaker, who did not know him. These agents and past forms are not replaced by a general future resolve to avoid evil.
The request that God hear a prayer and receive its cry remains unlinked because that common prayer-opening formula supplies no further distinctive correspondence here.

Wakefulness and a little bird alone on a roof are preserved. The read Proverbs candidate describes a bird flying down from its nest and an estranged person's enslavement; it does not establish the same solitary-rooftop image.
Enemies reproached the speaker and those praising him swore against him. The unusual praising and swearing roles are not rewritten as raging enemies or an unstated use of his name as a curse.

Ezra 9:13 says God lightened lawless deeds and gave deliverance, but does not expressly describe a lesser punishment. That proposed punitive equivalence remains uncredited; no sufficiently particular supported alternative is retained.

The rising mountains and descending plains reach their founded place. Genesis 8:5 describes mountain tops appearing as floodwaters recede, not mountains rising and plains descending. Identifying these scenes requires a claim the read texts do not establish.

Animals drinking and wild donkeys quenching thirst are stated specifically. A general account of wild donkeys or divine food provision would not establish a particular independent drinking comparison; none is retained.

The source combines birds nesting upon them with a voice from rocks. The antecedent and a sufficiently particular independent counterpart remain unsettled. The actual rock wording is preserved instead of supplying a tree-branch clause.

The sunrise-associated gathering and lying in enclosures is distinct from the creatures lying in ambush in Job 38:40. A generic shelter or animal-rest association does not establish the particular daylight pattern here.

The unit describes human work and labor until evening. An ordinary narrative of someone working or returning in the evening would be too general to establish a particular relationship; no supported comparison is retained.

The word arriving and the Lord's oracle putting Joseph through fire are not securely identified with a particular dream or fulfilled prediction in the read Genesis narrative. The timing, word and testing claims remain unresolved without importing a familiar interpretation.

The source describes instructing his rulers as himself and making his elders wise. Pharaoh calling Joseph discerning and appointing him over the house does not itself narrate teaching those groups. No explicit counterpart to these instructional acts is retained; the source's pronouns are preserved without an additional identification.

The request that a condemned person's prayer become sin is preserved. The checked Psalm 65:18 concerns non-hearing conditioned on injustice in the heart, and Proverbs 28:9 describes the law-rejecter's own abhorrence of his prayer. Neither establishes the same particular relationship; no supported counterpart is retained in this pass.

The clause describes the work of those slandering the speaker, from the Lord. Its grammatical relation is preserved without substituting a conventional reward-of-adversaries rendering; a particular independent counterpart remains unsettled.

The traveler drinks from a torrent and therefore lifts his head. The checked head-lifting psalm does not establish this drinking-and-result relationship or the identity of the traveler, and no passion or victory interpretation is supplied.

Taking the cup of salvation and calling on the Lord is preserved. A Eucharistic identification from the checked cup-of-blessing passage remains unestablished, and no particular supported cup counterpart is retained in this pass.

The petitions Save now and Prosper us now are preserved. The checked Gospel acclamation retains Hosanna rather than an English translation of it; no independent lexical verification or exact equivalence is claimed in this pass.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The target says the person who turns away from the law has himself abhorred his own prayer. It is not rewritten as God declaring the prayer an abomination; that proposed direct equivalence to the prayer becoming sin remains pending.

The source asks that the judged person's prayer become sin. Psalm 65:18 conditionally asks that the Lord not hear if the speaker was regarding injustice in his heart. These different relationships between wrongdoing and prayer leave only a broad association, not a sufficiently particular supported comparison.

Daniel explicitly refrains from anointing with oil and loses strength when he sees the vision. Psalm108 says the flesh was altered because of oil, not for lack of oil, and ties weakened knees to fasting. A direct equation of those causal details is not established.

Psalm3 names the Lord as the speaker's helper and head-lifter, but does not contain the torrent, drinking on a journey or the consequent head-lifting. The proposed specific restoration or victory interpretation of the whole source image remains unestablished.

Psalm28 says Lebanon is ground fine like the calf and the beloved like a young one-horned animal. It does not describe leaping mountains; a familiar skipping-Lebanon rendering cannot be substituted for the actual target.
Jeremiah promises purification for the souls of those who walk the good way. It does not say rest for your souls in this edition, so the proposed direct rest formula is not counted.
Paul explicitly identifies the blessed cup with participation in Christ's blood. The psalm names a cup of salvation without that identification, so an asserted identity of the cups is left pending.

The Gospel places Hosanna beside the explicit quotation of Psalm117:26, but it does not render Hosanna as Save now in the supplied English text. An exact lexical identification for source117:25 has not been independently checked and receives no credit.

The entry narrative contains branches and the preceding psalm verse's blessing, but it does not mention the altar horns or identify its procession as this festival. The proposed specific event identification remains pending despite the supported separate comparison with Leviticus' festival boughs.
